To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ultra-low-fire ZTTe ceramics have excellent dielectric properties at high-frequency, which is a good candidate for high-frequency and microwave application.
the ultra-low-fire dielectric ZTT thin film with good high-frequency and microwave dielectric properties was prepared by a radio frequency magnetron sputter method.
we have developed ultra-low-fire ZTNT ceramic composites and ZTT thin films with high εr, low tanδ, low leakage current density, ultra low processing temperature and high Q × fu values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an ultra-low-fire ceramic and ultra-low-fire ceramic thin film with excellent microwave properties.
the development of a low temperature, high frequency dielectric thin film.
the preparation and characterization of ultra-low-fire Zn2Te3-O8-30 %wt. Ti
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present work has successfully developed ultra-low-fire ZTTFs for high-frequency and microwave applications.
the ZTT ultra-low-fire dielectric thin film is a promising candidate for high-frequency and microwave applications.
the ultra-low-fire Zn2Te3-30 wt. % TiTe3O8 thin films are suitable for MMIC and microwave devices applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ultra-low-fire ZTTe ceramics have been successfully prepared by solid-state reaction method with high Q × ft and low τf.
the ultra-low-fire ceramic ZTT has the potential to become a promising candidate for high-frequency and microwave applications, such as high-temperature and high-frequency devices.
the ultra-low-fire dielectric thin film has the potential to be applied in the microwave devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we developed a new ultra-low-fire ZrTiTeO5 dielectric film, which is a good candidate for high-frequency and microwave applications.
the ZTT thin film can be used for ultra-low temperature integration in high frequency and microwave application.
the ultra-low-fire ceramic ZTT can be used as a high-κ dielectric material for the fabrication of high-κ gate oxide in MOSFET devices.
